newsitem.title: USA: Texaxo Inc crude pipeline shuts down.
newsitem.headline: Texaxo Inc crude pipeline shuts down.

text.p: Texaco Inc said a 50-mile portion of a key crude pipeline in California automatically shut early Tuesday after the pipeline ruptured and spilled 1,000 barrels of San Joaquin Valley heavy crude oil.
A spokeswoman for Texaco said the shut-down section of the pipeline has a throughput of 120,000 barrels-per-day.
The remaining portions of the line remained operational Tuesday. Total throughput on the pipeline is 340,000 bpd.
"We think within 24 hours we'll have this section of line repaired," the Texaco spokeswoman said.

The line, which has a 20-inch diameter, carries San Joaquin Valley crude between Bakersfield, Calif., oil reserves and San Francisco refineries. The crude has a 13-degree American Petroleum Institute (API) gravity rating.
The spokeswoman said she did "not have any information," on whether the rupture would disrupt supplies to San Francisco customers.
